candidate.educational_objective: Before deep sedation or anesthesia begins, the nurse verifies that required emergency airway equipment is immediately available and functional; a missing critical airway resource is a safety reason to delay the procedure until corrected.

options.A: Begin the procedure because emergency airway equipment is needed only when a difficult airway has already been predicted
options.B: Proceed if routine oxygen and suction are available, then obtain advanced airway equipment only if ventilation becomes difficult
options.C: Do not begin deep sedation until appropriate emergency airway equipment is immediately available and confirmed functional
options.D: Proceed if the client has no history of difficult intubation because prior uncomplicated anesthesia excludes an unexpected airway emergency

candidate.rationale: Sedation and anesthesia can progress to airway compromise unexpectedly, so appropriate emergency airway and resuscitation equipment must be immediately available and functional before care begins. ASA guidance for sedation/anesthesia settings requires emergency airway equipment to be available and functional, and NCSBN identifies inspection and safe use of client-care equipment as an RN safety responsibility. A previously uncomplicated airway, absence of a predicted difficult airway, or availability of oxygen and suction alone does not eliminate the need for full emergency airway readiness.
candidate.source_claim_supported: ASA states that settings providing sedation/anesthesia must have appropriate safety and resuscitative equipment, including emergency airway equipment, immediately available and functional, and that equipment must be checked/tested at accepted intervals.
candidate.source_document_title: Statement on Sedation & Anesthesia Administration in Dental Office-Based Settings
candidate.source_locator: Monitoring & Equipment; Resuscitative Measures & Protocols — appropriate monitors and safety equipment; emergency age-appropriate airway equipment immediately available and functional; equipment tested at accepted intervals
candidate.stem: Before a client receives deep sedation in a procedure room, the nurse discovers that the emergency airway equipment normally kept in the room has been removed for servicing and no replacement is immediately available. Which action is most appropriate?
